proof_scope: Acceptance-contract real CLI path: extracts source-backed requirements from local briefs and zip bundles, validates the pydantic acceptance_contract.bundle.v1 boundary, renders create_report.report.v1 artifacts through create-report, and fails closed on unsafe zip input.

claims.proves: acceptance-contract accepts local file and zip inputs, emits typed requirements/cases/open questions, creates draft-only immutable-goal text, validates the bundle boundary, delegates report rendering to create-report, and rejects unsafe zip traversal. It also proves the ensure preflight creates/validates frozen contracts, rejects stale source hashes, and refuses repository roots by default. It proves quick brief plus numeric policy bundle derives the typed-scalar PII case that oai-trial missed. It proves the derived contract includes canonical-equivalence matching, not just typed-scalar wording. It proves the roundtable-driven all-format trap and lossy numeric conversion clauses are derived too.
claims.does_not_prove: that extracted requirements are semantically complete, human-approved, sufficient for a real client contract, or that Battle has executed the resulting bundle.

capability_claims.description: The skill extracts explicit must/shall/acceptance/fail-closed requirements from supplied local source files.
The skill renders a create-report-backed report from validated JSON.
The skill rejects unsafe zip members instead of extracting path traversal entries.
The skill validates an existing acceptance bundle, creates it when missing, and rejects stale source hashes.
The skill refuses repository roots by default so implementation files cannot become the acceptance source.
The skill derives an executable typed-scalar PII acceptance case from a quick brief plus numeric-looking policy values in the supplied bundle.

derived_from.requirement: The same synthetic identity can appear in every format; policy.json contains numeric-looking sensitive_values[].value entries.

capability_claims.description: The skill derives a canonical-equivalence acceptance case so formatted policy strings cannot evade typed JSON/SQLite numeric scalar detection.

derived_from.requirement: The same synthetic identity can appear in every format; policy.json supplies sensitive values by type and value.

The system must remove customer phone numbers in every representation.
Valid CSV rows must accept non-sensitive literals unchanged.
Outputs must not leak policy values.

$ROOT/skills/acceptance-contract/run.sh extract $tmp/brief.md --out $tmp/out --project-name demo --goal-mode create >/tmp/acceptance-contract-eval-file-receipt.json && python3 - <<'PY' $tmp/out/acceptance_bundle.json

assert len(bundle['requirements'])==3
assert len(bundle['acceptance_cases'])==3
assert bundle['immutable_goal']['mutation_policy']=='draft_only_human_approval_required'

PY

cases.name: unsafe-zip-fails-closed
command:
ROOT=/home/graham/workspace/experiments/agent-skills; tmp=/tmp/acceptance-contract-eval-unsafe; rm -rf $tmp; mkdir -p $tmp; python3 - <<'PY' $tmp/bad.zip
import sys, zipfile
with zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1], 'w') as zf:
    zf.writestr('../brief.txt', 'The system must reject traversal.\n')
PY
if $ROOT/skills/acceptance-contract/run.sh extract $tmp/bad.zip --out $tmp/out >$tmp/stdout 2>$tmp/stderr; then exit 9; fi; python3 - <<'PY' $tmp/stderr /tmp/acceptance-contract-eval-unsafe-proof.json
import json, pathlib, sys
err=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()
proof={'status':'PASS' if 'unsafe zip member' in err else 'FAIL', 'stderr_contains_unsafe_zip_member':'unsafe zip member' in err}
pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).write_text(json.dumps(proof))
assert proof['status']=='PASS'
print('unsafe zip rejected PASS')
PY

cases.name: quick-brief-policy-derives-typed-scalar-pii-case
command:
ROOT=/home/graham/workspace/experiments/agent-skills; tmp=/tmp/acceptance-contract-eval-typed-scalar; rm -rf $tmp; mkdir -p $tmp/spec; printf 'The system must anonymize CSV, JSON, UTF-8 text, and SQLite database files. The same synthetic identity can appear in every format.\n' >$tmp/spec/TRIAL_BRIEF.md; printf '{"sensitive_values":[{"type":"phone","value":"5550102000"}]}\n' >$tmp/spec/policy.json; $ROOT/skills/acceptance-contract/run.sh ensure $tmp/spec --out $tmp/out --project-name demo >/tmp/acceptance-contract-eval-typed-scalar-receipt.json && python3 - <<'PY' $tmp/out/acceptance_bundle.json /tmp/acceptance-contract-eval-typed-scalar-proof.json
import json, pathlib, sys
b=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
statements=[r['statement'] for r in b['requirements']]
proof={'typed_scalar_case': any('typed JSON or SQLite scalar' in s for s in statements), 'canonical_equivalence_case': any('canonical equivalence' in s and 'CSV cells' in s for s in statements), 'cross_format_trap_case': any('seeded across every in-scope format' in s for s in statements), 'lossy_numeric_case': any('leading-zero loss' in s and 'float precision loss' in s for s in statements), 'requirements': len(statements)}
pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).write_text(json.dumps(proof))
assert proof['typed_scalar_case'] and proof['canonical_equivalence_case'] and proof['cross_format_trap_case'] and proof['lossy_numeric_case']
print('typed scalar derivation PASS')
PY
